result.title: Decode Early, Verify Late: Streaming Offline Speech Recognizers Without Accuracy Loss
result.summary: Voice agents need accurate transcripts soon after a user stops speaking. We propose Decode Early, Verify Late (DEVL), a training-free framework for streaming inference with offline ASR models. The server keeps partial transcripts as drafts and verifies the latest against the complete audio in one forward pass at turn end. Under stated input and decoding conditions, the final equals the model's greedy offline output in exact arithmetic. We adapt DEVL to four model families. In our five-recognizer comparison, 95-100% of final transcripts are byte-identical to the offline transcripts, WER stays within 0.13 points of offline, and single-stream time to final falls 1.5-7.3x. Serving Qwen3-ASR-1.7B on one A100, DEVL returns finals a median 22-26 ms after turn end at up to 64 streams, 2.7-3.9x sooner than the official streaming mode. It is the only system we tested that meets a 100 ms p99 target, up to 80 streams on Pipecat-STT and 64 on WildASR.

AI.brief_summary: 提出免训练的 DEVL 框架，让离线 ASR 模型支持流式输出：服务端先保留部分转录作为草稿，在话轮结束时用完整音频一次前向验证最新草稿，并在给定输入与解码条件下声称最终结果与离线 greedy 输出一致；在五种识别器上报告一致率、WER 与时延收益。
AI.relevance_reason: 「先出草稿、后用完整证据复核」的流程可为 LVR 中候选推理状态与视觉证据的验证、停止决策提供方法线索，但论文属语音识别且不涉及视觉 latent 推理，其精确一致条件能否迁移尚需核查。
